'''Joel Hans Embiid''' ({{respell|joh|EL|'}} {{respell|EM|beed}}; born March 16, 1994) is a Cameroonian [[basketball]] player who recently completed his college career for the [[Kansas Jayhawks men's basketball|University of Kansas]].<ref>[http://sportsillustrated.cnn.com/nba/news/20130926/nba-draft-big-board-2014-andrew-wiggins/ 2014 NBA Big Board: Wiggins leads deepest draft in years]</ref><ref>[http://insider.espn.go.com/nbadraft/results/top100/_/year/2014 Chad Ford's Top 100 - 2014]</ref><ref>[http://www.kansascity.com/2013/10/25/4576844/in-joel-embiid-the-kansas-jayhawks.html In Joel Embiid, the Kansas Jayhawks have a star-to-be from Cameroon]</ref> 

==High school career==
Embiid was discovered by [[Luc Mbah a Moute]], a professional player with the [[Minnesota Timberwolves]].<ref>[http://www.kansascity.com/sports/college/big-12/university-of-kansas/article343459/Report-Kansas-basketball-star-Joel-Embiid-will-enter-NBA-Draft.html Report: Kansas basketball star Joel Embiid will enter NBA Draft]</ref>

Embiid attended the Rock School, a Christian academy, in [[Gainesville, Florida]], and was a five-star recruit by [[Rivals.com]].<ref>{{cite web|title=KU’s Embiid grows as a basketball player|url=http://www.kansascity.com/2013/12/09/4682046/kus-embiid-grows-as-a-basketball.html}}</ref><ref>[http://sports.yahoo.com/footballrecruiting/basketball/recruiting/player-Joel-Embiid-143044 Rivals.com]</ref> He committed to Kansas in November 2012.<ref>[http://espn.go.com/college-sports/recruiting/basketball/mens/story/_/id/8627432/joel-embiid-makes-verbal-commitment-kansas-jayhawks Kansas lands recruit Joel Embiid]</ref> Embiid has been compared to NBA greats such as [[Hakeem Olajuwon]] and [[Tim Duncan]].<ref>[http://cjonline.com/sports/2013-09-26/embiids-potential-has-ku-fans-dreaming Embiid's potential has KU fans dreaming]</ref>

==College career==
On February 13, 2014, Embiid was named one of the 30 finalists for the [[Naismith College Player of the Year]].<ref>{{cite web|title=2013-14 Men's Naismith Trophy Midseason 30|url=http://www.naismithawards.com/PressBox/ArticleView/tabid/209/ArticleId/8/2013-14-Mens-Naismith-Trophy-Midseason-30.aspx|work=Naismith Awards|accessdate=February 14, 2014|date=February 13, 2014}}</ref>

On March 11, 2014, ESPN announced that Embiid was expected to miss the Big 12 tournament, and was "unlikely to play the first weekend of the NCAA Tournament" due to a stress fracture in his back.<ref>[http://espn.go.com/mens-college-basketball/story/_/id/10585990/joel-embiid-kansas-jayhawks-indefinitely-getting-second-opinion Joel Embiid out indefinitely]</ref> Kansas lost in the third round of the tournament, before Embiid could return. In 2013–14, he played 28 games, averaging 11.2 points, 8.1 rebounds, 1.4 assists and 2.6 blocks in 23.1 minutes per game.<ref>[http://www.sports-reference.com/cbb/players/joel-embiid-1.html Joel Embiid Stats]</ref>

==NBA==
On April 9, 2014, Embiid declared for the [[2014 NBA draft]], forgoing his final three years of college eligibility.<ref>[http://nba.si.com/2014/04/09/joel-embiid-declares-draft-kansas/ Kansas’ Joel Embiid declares for 2014 NBA draft]</ref> On June 20, 2014, Embiid underwent surgery on a broken foot which requires four-to-six months of recovery.<ref>[http://msn.foxsports.com/ohio/story/nba-draft-how-far-will-embiid-fall-062114 No. 1 question: How far will Joel Embiid fall?]</ref>
